title: Turning archives into intelligence: Vizrt and DeepVA introduce AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One media asset management
body_html:
Why This Matters Right Now

The pressure to optimize media archives and streamline content delivery workflows has never been more intense for broadcast and media companies. As the volume of content grows, so does the complexity of managing and delivering it efficiently. Manual metadata tagging, a crucial step in the content preparation workflow, is often a time-consuming and labor-intensive process that can lead to errors and inconsistencies. This is where AI-driven metadata enrichment comes into play, promising to reduce manual quality control effort and enhance the search and retrieval capabilities within media archives. For broadcast engineers, operations leads, and CTOs, the introduction of AI-driven metadata enrichment in media asset management systems like Viz One is a significant development that warrants attention. The ability to automate metadata tagging can have a profound impact on the operational efficiency of broadcast and media companies. By reducing the time and resources spent on manual metadata entry, media organizations can reallocate their resources to more strategic tasks, such as content creation and programming. This, in turn, can lead to faster content delivery, lower infrastructure costs, and improved operational ROI. Moreover, the accuracy and consistency of metadata are critical for ensuring seamless content delivery and discovery, making AI-driven metadata enrichment a key factor in the pursuit of operational excellence. The integration of AI-driven metadata enrichment in media asset management systems also speaks to the broader trend of leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to optimize broadcast and media workflows. As the media industry continues to evolve, the need for efficient, scalable, and automated solutions will only continue to grow. For technical teams, staying ahead of the curve and embracing innovative technologies like AI-driven metadata enrichment will be essential for remaining competitive and delivering high-quality content to audiences.

Under the Hood: How It Actually Works

The AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One media asset management system utilizes artificial intelligence to automate the process of metadata tagging. This development enables the system to support automated metadata tagging using AI, potentially reducing egress costs and enhancing data integrity. The integration of AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One is designed to work seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, leveraging object storage and microservices architecture to ensure scalability and flexibility. The use of Kubernetes for container orchestration and API orchestration for workflow automation further enhances the security and integrity of the system. The technical implication of this integration is that Viz One now supports automated metadata tagging using AI, which can be integrated with object storage, such as S3, for scalable media storage and workflow automation. The solution is compatible with industry-standard protocols, such as ST 2110 for ingest and NMOS for device discovery and control. This compatibility ensures smooth integration with other systems and devices, making it easier to incorporate AI-driven metadata enrichment into existing broadcast and media workflows. The AI-driven metadata enrichment solution requires a minimum of 16 GB RAM and 4 CPU cores for optimal performance, with a recommended network bandwidth of 1 GbE for data transfer. The solution is dependent on the presence of a compatible MAM system, such as Viz One. The technical specifications of the solution highlight the importance of careful planning and deployment to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance.

In a real broadcast operation, the integration of AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One media asset management system can have a significant impact on the content preparation workflow. For instance, in a newsroom environment, the automated metadata tagging process can enable faster and more accurate search and retrieval of content, allowing journalists and producers to focus on creating high-quality stories rather than manually tagging metadata. The AI-driven metadata enrichment can also enhance the collaboration among teams, as accurate and consistent metadata ensures that all stakeholders have access to the same information, reducing errors and inconsistencies. In a live production environment, the AI-driven metadata enrichment can facilitate the efficient management of large volumes of content, enabling producers to quickly locate and retrieve specific clips or assets. The automated metadata tagging process can also reduce the time and resources spent on manual quality control, allowing technical teams to focus on more strategic tasks, such as optimizing the production workflow and ensuring high-quality content delivery.
